content.text:
Found it: `tailwind-css/src/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.mdx` — "Dynamic class names" section (lines 65–98).

Tailwind scans your source as plain text — it can't evaluate `{{ Vite::image('hero.jpg') }}` interpolation, so `bg-[url('{{ ... }}')]` is never a real, complete string in your source. It won't be detected as a class and no CSS is generated for it.

Your fix (inline `style="background-image: url(...)"`) is the correct workaround — arbitrary values only work with complete, static strings, not dynamic/interpolated ones.

Tailwind scans your source as plain text — it can't evaluate `{{ Vite::image('hero.jpg') }}` interpolation, so `bg-[url('{{ ... }}')]` is never a real, complete string in your source. It won't be detected as a class and no CSS is generated for it.

Your fix (inline `style="background-image: url(...)"`) is the correct workaround — arbitrary values only work with complete, static strings, not dynamic/interpolated ones.
